title: Working with strings
description:
Complete the methods:

```csharp
public static string Initials(string fullName)               // "ada king lovelace" gives "A.K.L."
public static string Slug(string title)                      // "  Hello, World! C# 13 " gives "hello-world-c-13"
public static string PriceLine(string item, decimal price)   // item left in 12 characters, price right in 8 with 2 decimals
public static int CountVowels(string text)                   // a, e, i, o, u in either case
```

- `Initials` ignores extra spaces between and around the names.
- `Slug` keeps letters and digits in lower case, turns every run of other characters into one `-`, and has no `-` at either end.
- `PriceLine("Tea", 2.5m)` is `"Tea             2.50"`: 12 characters for the item, then 8 for the price. Write the price with a `.` whatever the computer's culture: `price.ToString("F2", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)`.
hints: `Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries)` drops the empty pieces that runs of spaces would give.

`foreach (char c in text) { ... }` runs its body once for each character, and `if (test) { ... } else { ... }` picks one of two branches (both come properly in lesson 1.05). `char.IsLetterOrDigit(c)` is true for a letter or a digit, like `char.IsLetter` and `char.IsDigit` together.
For `Slug`, walk the characters and remember whether a separator was seen since the last letter or digit; write the `-` only when the next letter or digit arrives and something is already written.
